findings.title: Missing foreign key enforcement for comments
findings.explanation: The SQLite database is created without enabling foreign key constraints, so inserting a comment with a non‑existent ticket_id will succeed. This can corrupt data integrity because comments may reference tickets that do not exist, even though the service layer checks for ticket existence.

evidence.quote:
self._db = sqlite3.connect(path)
self._db.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
self._db.execute(SCHEMA)
self._db.execute(COMMENTS_SCHEMA)
"INSERT INTO comments (ticket_id, author, body, created_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)"

findings.verification_note: SQLite connection is created without enabling foreign key constraints, so the foreign key in COMMENTS_SCHEMA is not enforced.

findings.title: Rule: public functions have type hints and a one-line docstring that says what they return or raise
findings.explanation: The `list_comments` method's docstring does not specify its return value (a list of Comment objects), which breaches the rule requiring docstrings to state what the function returns.

evidence.quote: Public functions have type hints and a one-line docstring that says what they return or raise.

findings.verification_note: list_comments has a one-line docstring that does not describe its return value, violating the rule requiring such a description.

limitations: The codebase does not include the part that renders comments to users, so the actual XSS impact depends on whether the output is escaped.

criteria.text: Any user can add a comment to an existing ticket.
criteria.explanation: The add_comment method accepts any author string and does not enforce permission checks, allowing any user to add a comment to an existing ticket.

evidence.quote: def add_comment(self, ticket_id: int, author: str, body: str) -> Comment:

criteria.text: An empty or whitespace-only comment is rejected.
criteria.explanation: The implementation strips whitespace and raises ValueError when the resulting body is empty, rejecting empty or whitespace‑only comments.

evidence.quote:
if not body:
    raise ValueError("a comment cannot be empty")

criteria.text: A comment is at most 2000 characters.
criteria.explanation: MAX_COMMENT is defined as 2000 and the add_comment method raises ValueError when the comment length exceeds this limit, enforcing the maximum length.

evidence.quote:
if len(body) > MAX_COMMENT:
    raise ValueError(f"a comment is at most {MAX_COMMENT} characters")

criteria.text: A ticket's comments are listed oldest first.
criteria.explanation: The comments method returns results from store.list_comments, which queries comments ordered by id (auto‑increment), ensuring oldest‑first ordering.

evidence.quote: SELECT * FROM comments WHERE ticket_id = ? ORDER BY id

finding.title: Stored XSS risk due to unsanitized comment body
finding.explanation: User-provided comment body is stored and later may be rendered without HTML escaping, allowing injection of malicious scripts.

dismissed.reason: The code only stores the comment body; no rendering logic is provided to confirm an XSS risk.

finding.title: Rule: public functions have type hints and a one-line docstring that says what they return or raise
finding.explanation: The `add_comment` method has a one-line docstring that mentions the raised exception but does not state what the function returns, violating the rule that public functions must have a docstring describing their return value or raised exceptions.

evidence.quote: """Add a comment to an existing ticket. Raises ValueError if it is empty or longer than MAX_COMMENT."""
Public functions have type hints and a one-line docstring that says what they return or raise.

dismissed.reason: The docstring for add_comment mentions the raised exception, satisfying the rule that a docstring must state what is returned or raised.
